addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- crypto-privacy-reviewer: Cryptography and privacy expert that reviews code, validates assumptions, and generates test cases. NOT prefixed with gsd- so it survives GSD updates. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## pencil
The Pencil MCP server is the editor for .pen design files (web/mobile apps and websites). Use it to read, generate, and validate designs.

.pen files are encrypted: access them only via "pencil" MCP tools — never use Read or Grep on .pen files. Follow each tool's input schema exactly.

Always call get_editor_state(include_schema: true) if you don't have the current .pen file schema in the context. Knowing the schema is required to use any other Pencil MCP tool.

Tools: get_editor_state, get_guidelines, batch_get, batch_design, snapshot_layout, get_screenshot, get_variables, export_nodes, export_html.

- code-review: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes — Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/PRD asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".
- codebase-design: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.
- design-an-interface: Generate multiple radically different interface designs for a module using parallel sub-agents. Use when user wants to design an API, explore interface options, compare module shapes, or mentions "design it twice".
- diagnosing-bugs: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.
- domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when the user wants to pin down domain terminology or a ubiquitous language, record an architectural decision, or when another skill needs to maintain the domain model.
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- git-guardrails-claude-code: Set up Claude Code hooks to block dangerous git commands (push, reset --hard, clean, branch -D, etc.) before they execute. Use when user wants to prevent destructive git operations, add git safety hooks, or block git push/reset in Claude Code.
- grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
- gsd-dev-preferences: Load developer preferences into this session
- migrate-to-shoehorn: Migrate test files from `as` type assertions to @total-typescript/shoehorn. Use when user mentions shoehorn, wants to replace `as` in tests, or needs partial test data.
- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the Obsidian vault with wikilinks and index notes. Use when user wants to find, create, or organize notes in Obsidian.
- prototype: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.
- qa: Interactive QA session where user reports bugs or issues conversationally, and the agent files GitHub issues. Explores the codebase in the background for context and domain language. Use when user wants to report bugs, do QA, file issues conversationally, or mentions "QA session".
- request-refactor-plan: Create a detailed refactor plan with tiny commits via user interview, then file it as a GitHub issue. Use when user wants to plan a refactor, create a refactoring RFC, or break a refactor into safe incremental steps.
- research: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.
- resolving-merge-conflicts: Use when you need to resolve an in-progress git merge/rebase conflict.
- review: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes — Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/PRD asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".
- scaffold-exercises: Create exercise directory structures with sections, problems, solutions, and explainers that pass linting. Use when user wants to scaffold exercises, create exercise stubs, or set up a new course section.
- setup-pre-commit: Set up Husky pre-commit hooks with lint-staged (Prettier), type checking, and tests in the current repo. Use when user wants to add pre-commit hooks, set up Husky, configure lint-staged, or add commit-time formatting/typechecking/testing.
- tdd: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
- crypto-privacy-review: Review code for cryptographic security, generate test cases and edge cases
- resolve-pr-reviews: Resolve PR Review Comments
- ship: Ship
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

=== #861 ===
core: add the settings-name KDF edge and regenerate the catalog KATs
## Dependencies
=== #862 ===
engine: freeze the content format and land the engine-side KAT
- `InvalidManifest`'s free-form reasons are promoted to real `check()` strings — the prerequisite for the engine KAT.
## Dependencies
=== #863 ===

## Dependencies

## Dependencies
Blocked by the op-record format slice.
=== #866 ===
engine: publish the remaining four op kinds under the reference-ordering law
## Dependencies
Blocked by the folder-create vertical.
=== #867 ===
engine: drain failure policy for dead-letter, blocked, and abandonment
**The `Blocked` class for an over-quota 413** (#841).
- `ScriptedHttp` returns a 413 carrying `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`; the op enters `Blocked`, holds the head, keeps its reservation, and resumes on a quota probe reporting room.
## Dependencies
Blocked by the five-op-kind drain.
=== #868 ===
engine: write file content end to end
**Per-block staging** (#828). A version stages as N+1 independent blocks, each keyed by its own content address; the op carries the root's, which is also the version's `contentCid`. Leaf keys are derivable by decoding the staged root. Blocks are **CID-verified on read from staging** — the read path already hard-rejects a mismatch, so an unverified upload turns bit-rot into a permanently unreadable published version.
**The per-version content key** (#818). Staged sealed, HPKE-to-self under the owner `enc-subkey`, riding the op. `enc-subkey` comes from the loginSecret, so it is epoch-independent and available exactly when a drain can run. Epoch rides the AAD as a value, not a key input. Needs a distinct struct tag and the `contentCid` in the sealed payload. A key-open failure dead-letters the op and **releases** its blocks.
## Dependencies
Blocked by the drain failure-policy slice and by the content format freeze.
=== #869 ===
engine: cancel an upload and collect orphaned staged blocks
- Requires a **block-boundary yield** in the drain's upload loop. Without it the guarantee collapses to "cancel only works before the op starts".
- Cascade keys on whether the node survives: a cancelled **create** takes every later queued op on that node; a cancelled `UpdateContent` takes nothing, since versions are independent full writes.
## Dependencies
Blocked by the content write slice.
=== #870 ===
engine: publish and resolve the vault settings record
## Dependencies
Blocked by the settings KDF edge and by the folder-create vertical.
=== #871 ===
engine: wire the pin-provider layer across all three modes
## Dependencies
Blocked by the content write slice and the settings record slice.
=== #872 ===
engine: prune old versions and reclaim their bytes
**Three correctness prerequisites first.**
- **#849** — prune retires only the DAG root, orphaning every sealed leaf. The expansion is the hard prerequisite of everything below. Two constraints on its shape: `root + leaf_cids` **cannot be one call** (`MAX_BATCH = 1000` and a 1 GiB version is 1025 targets at the frozen 1 MiB framing, so partial retire is normal at exactly `max_file_bytes`), and **leaves retire before their root**.
## Dependencies
Blocked by the pin-provider layer slice.
=== #873 ===
web: wire file upload through the facade write handles
#807 keeps download and static preview, which #811 already unblocked. This carries upload alone.
## Dependencies
Blocked by the content write slice, and by the upload-side op-progress surface — `OpPhase` has only `Download*` variants (`facade.rs:438-445`) and `emit_op_progress` hardcodes `op_id: None` (`facade.rs:1524`). That phase set is still fog on #813.

| Issue | Branch | Scope |

I'll report each agent's result as it completes, then run `/code-review` over the combined work.

## 1. `blueprint/engine.md`

**Op queue / intent ops**

- `/…/blueprint/engine.md:47` (what died): `| mkdir+uploads-only offline journal | #33 D6 — every mutation rides the durable op queue |`
- `:56` module map: `- **sync** — focus-window scheduler, staleness ladder, op queue, rebase.`
- `:189-191` **State law**: "rendered state = last-known-good remote snapshot ⊕ pending-op overlay, single owner; the op queue is the only local divergence (#33 D6)."
- `:208-215` **Ops**: "every mutation is an intent op — `create`, `delete`, `rename`, `relink`, `updateContent` — carrying its base sequence, journaled FIFO in the durable op queue (all mutations, both platforms). An intra-scope `relink` is a pure relink; a cross-scope `relink` re-seals the moved subtree at the destination scope's epoch, and one that leaves a granted source scope is a scope-exit rotation trigger for the source (#26 D1/D7). Replay is FIFO in performed order through the standard rebase, and rebases only onto gate-passing state (#33 D5–D7)."
- `:221-229` the five per-op rebase rules table (#33 D5).
- `:495` facade: "commands (the intent ops, grant/rotation/share actions, auth, manual refresh)".

**Staging store seam** — `/…/blueprint/engine.md:81`, in the Host seams table:

```
| **StagingStore**      | Durable op queue + staged upload bytes (profile-scoped budget)  | IndexedDB + OPFS | Local journal |
```

Note the seam owns *both* the op queue and the staged bytes. Related: `:63` `- **content** — chunk framing, staging, the pin-provider layer.`

**Staging budget** — `:198-202` (part of the profile, below) and `:233-235`.

**Line ~231-233, the byte-release rule** (exact text, `:231-235`):

```
Terminally unrebasable ops (e.g. access revoked while offline) **dead-letter**
with a visible notice and staged bytes preserved; nothing is silently dropped
(#33 D6). Web reaches full offline parity: uploads stage into OPFS/IndexedDB
behind the profile budget (past it, only new uploads fail fast; metadata ops
queue unbounded).
```

So the rule is: staged bytes are **preserved**, never released, on dead-letter; and budget exhaustion fails **only new uploads** fast — metadata ops queue unbounded. There is no other byte-release/GC rule in engine.md (the only GC-ish mention of staging is in testing.md's seam conformance kit: "StagingStore ordering and orphan GC").

**`SyncTimingProfile`** — the type name never appears in engine.md; it is written as "sync timing profile". `/…/blueprint/engine.md:198-202`:

```
- **Sync timing profile** (environment-scoped): record TTL, poll cadence,
  staleness thresholds, offline staging budget, escalation window, and the
  pointer-consult interval that bounds the read-only-survivor residual
  (#38 residuals). The profile is the CI-DX hook — dev/CI values make
  cross-client e2e flows testable at speed (#33 D3).
```

Other profile references: `:119-121` (TTL "production 1 minute; dev/CI 1–5 s; never a library default"), `:216-217` (escalation window), `:508` (migration-window closure "proposed as a sync-timing-profile constant"), `:512` ("**Sweep cadence** — the idle-cadence value joins the sync timing profile.").

**Storage policy** — **no mention.** Grep for `storage polic` in `blueprint/engine.md` returns nothing. The nearest policy statements are `:135` "Retirement: retire = remove my registry rows; timing is engine policy (#34 D4)"; `:55` "trust-violation policy"; and `:488-490` "Retention default: keep all versions within quota, with an explicit user-initiated prune op. Exact chunk size and retention knobs are open edges below." — i.e. retention/chunking policy is an **open edge** (`:510-511`: "**Chunk size, DAG shape, retention defaults** — the judgment above needs numbers; freeze alongside the KAT manifest and testing strategy.").

**Determinism / injected-policy rules** — engine.md states the injection law but not the word "determinism":

- `:30-31` "Hosts inject every capability as a constructor seam trait; a missing seam is a compile error, not a silent behavior gap (#26 D8)."
- `:40` "| Optional floor injection (omit `rotationHighWater`, get nothing) | #26 D4 / #33 D7 — floors are a required constructor argument |"; reinforced at `:173-174` "`FloorStore` is a required constructor argument, fail-closed on regression."
- `:92-93` "Entropy and timestamps are engine inputs to core's pure functions: the clock comes from `Scheduler`, entropy from per-target `getrandom` wiring (core.md)."
- `:229` deterministic dual-link loser; `:69-71` "The constructor takes the seam set whole… Traits move opaque bytes and events — no seam holds logic."

The explicit determinism law lives in testing.md law 3 (below).

---

## 2. `blueprint/testing.md`

**Law 1 (the CI gate law)** — `/…/blueprint/testing.md:24-29`:

```
1. **A suite that does not block a merge does not exist.** v1's evidence:
   `apps/web` had a vitest config and no CI runner; `.spec.ts` files sat
   silently outside a `.test.ts` include; web and desktop e2e ran only
   post-merge, discovering regressions after they landed; an entire auth
   Playwright scaffold (`tests/e2e/`) was never even committed. Every v2 suite
   is wired into a named gate in this doc the day it lands, or it is deleted.
```

Law 3 (`:38-43`) is the determinism rule: "**Determinism is injected, not hoped for.** Core takes entropy, time, and policy as parameters; the engine takes every capability as a seam trait; the sync timing profile is environment-scoped."

**Suite map** — `:60-193`, sections: `crates/core — KATs and property tests` (`:62`, manifest job merge-blocking native+WASM `:68-74`, property tests `:75-81`); `crates/engine — seam fakes and the simulation harness` (`:83-117`, including the mandatory scenario matrix — the last bullet `:111-113` is "the offline queue — FIFO replay through rebase, dead-letter on revoked-while-offline with staged bytes preserved, staging-budget fail-fast"); `The contract suite — the live API gate` (`:119`); `Host suites` (`:142`, incl. seam conformance kits `:151-156`: "StagingStore ordering and orphan GC"); `E2E` (`:173`).

**The named gate "Engine Tests"** — **testing.md does not name a gate "Engine Tests".** Its CI gates section (`:195-204`) is a three-tier table; the PR-gate row (`:202`) says "cargo workspace tests (core KATs + property layer, engine simulation, fuse op core)". The name "Engine Tests" exists only in `ci.yml` (see §4).

---

## 3. `CONTEXT.md` — ubiquitous-language entries

Exact terms present:

- **Op queue** — `/…/CONTEXT.md:52`: "**Op queue** — the durable FIFO journal of intent ops every mutation rides. Offline replay and online CAS rebase re-apply ops through the same path."
- **Epoch** — `:13`: "**Epoch** — a scope-relative rotation counter. Every sealed body carries a plaintext, AAD-bound **epoch tag** `{scope, epoch}`."
- **Scope** — `:8`: "**Scope** — a derivation domain: the set of nodes keyed from one random scope seed. The vault root is the initial scope; every grant on an interior folder and every rotation creates or re-seeds one." (Also **Scope root** `:9`, **Scope pointer** `:42`.)

Terms **absent** as glossary entries:

- **staging** — no entry. Appears only inside other definitions: `:49` **Sync timing profile** — "record TTL, poll cadence, staleness thresholds, offline **staging budget**, escalation window"; `:57` **Dead-letter** — "surfaced to the user with any **staged content preserved** rather than silently dropped".
- **staging budget** — no standalone entry; only the phrase "offline staging budget" at `:49`.
- **owner tag** — no such term anywhere in the repo. The tag vocabulary is **Blinded tag** (`:35`) and **epoch tag** (`:13`); owner-side entries are **Owner blob** (`:15`), **Owner write blob** (`:16`), **Owner seed cache** (`:17`).
- **content cid / contentCid** — no CONTEXT.md entry. `contentCid` appears only in `blueprint/core.md:108` (read-body versions list `[{contentCid, contentKey, size, modifiedAt}]`), `blueprint/engine.md:487`, `blueprint/engine.md:465` and `blueprint/api.md:52` (`contentCids[]` in batch register). Closest glossary neighbor: **Content key** (`:10`).
- **authored time** — no entry, and no `authoredAt` anywhere. The time fields in the model are `createdAt`/`modifiedAt` ("injected timestamps", `blueprint/core.md:107`). CONTEXT.md uses "Authored"/"self-authored" only as verbs (`:16`, `:17`).

---

## 4. `.github/workflows/` — the `Engine Tests` job

File: `/…/.github/workflows/ci.yml` (workflow `name: CI`, `ci.yml:7`).

- **Job id**: `engine` (`ci.yml:352`), **`name: Engine Tests`** (`ci.yml:353`).
- **Runs on**: `ubuntu-latest`; `needs: [changes, lint]`; gated `if: !failure() && !cancelled() && needs.changes.outputs.rust == 'true'` (`ci.yml:354-358`).
- **Steps**: checkout, cargo cache, then a single test step (`ci.yml:373-377`):

```yaml
      # Engine unit tests plus every seam conformance kit executed against
      # its in-memory fake (the test-kit feature activates via the crate's
      # self dev-dependency).
      - name: Engine tests and seam conformance kits
        run: cargo test -p cipherbox-engine
```

So: it runs **`cargo test -p cipherbox-engine` only** — not `--workspace`, and **not** `cargo test -p cipherbox-core`.

**Triggers/paths**: the workflow fires on `pull_request: branches: [main]` (`ci.yml:9-11`). The `engine` job is path-filtered through the `changes` job's `rust` filter (`ci.yml:40-46`): `crates/**`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `.cargo/config.toml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Note the filter is `crates/**` broadly — a `crates/core`-only change still triggers `Engine Tests`.

**Does `crates/core` run in a named required gate?** Yes, in several:

- `core-kats` / **`name: Core KATs (native + WASM)`** (`ci.yml:385-386`) — the dedicated core gate. Steps: `ci.yml:432-436` regenerate-and-diff (`cargo run -p cipherbox-core --example kat_gen` then `git diff --exit-code -- crates/core/kat` plus a `git status --porcelain` check); `:439` `cargo test -p cipherbox-core`; `:442` `cargo test -p cipherbox-core --target wasm32-wasip1`; `:448` `cargo test -p cipherbox-core --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --test kat_manifest --test codec_props --test ipns_props --test seal_props`; `:453` `cargo test -p cipherbox-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`; `:463-469` a getrandom-tripwire on core's production graph.
- `cargo-linux` / `Cargo Check & Test (Linux)` (`ci.yml:317-318`), `cargo-macos` (`:542-543`), `cargo-windows` (`:569-570`) each run `cargo test --workspace --exclude cipherbox-desktop --exclude cipherbox-contract` (`:350`, `:567`, `:594`), which includes `cipherbox-core` and `cipherbox-engine`.

**fmt / clippy gates:** yes.

- `ci.yml:338-339` `- name: Cargo fmt` / `run: cargo fmt --all --check` (in `cargo-linux`).
- `ci.yml:346-347` `- name: Cargo clippy` / `run: cargo clippy --workspace --exclude cipherbox-desktop --exclude cipherbox-contract --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- Excluded crates own their own: `ci.yml:683-686` contract crate (`cargo fmt -p cipherbox-contract --check`, `cargo clippy -p cipherbox-contract --all-targets -- -D warnings`); `ci.yml:789` / `:795` desktop shell.

## 5. `crates/core` KAT regime — is the struct-tag registry frozen in a committed manifest?

**Yes — in three committed places, all of which must change for a tenth tag.**

1. **The manifest**: `/…/crates/core/kat/manifest.json`, top-level key `structureTags`. Shape is a flat `{name: tagByte}` object (serde_json orders keys deterministically):

```json

  "ascent-link": 5, "grant-blob": 3, "history-link": 6, "mailbox-payload": 8,
  "owner-blob": 4, "owner-write-blob": 9, "pointer-payload": 7,
  "read-body": 1, "write-body": 2
```

### Encoding at rest — **two files per op, and the envelope is plaintext JSON**

```
<journal_dir>/<id>.json   # serde_json JSON, 0o600, fsync'd, then parent dir fsync'd
<journal_dir>/<id>.bin    # raw AES-256-GCM ciphertext sidecar, 0o600, streamed in 1 MiB chunks
```

`WriteQueue::put`, `put_with_sidecar`, `sidecar_path_for(id)`, `remove(id)`. `id` = hex of 16 random bytes.

**The op record is NOT sealed as a whole.** This is the single biggest divergence from the v2 sketch `owner_tag || content_root_cid? || sealed(op)`. v1 does **field-level** confidentiality inside a cleartext JSON envelope:

| Field | At-rest form |
|---|---|
| `id`, `vault_root_ipns`, `retries`, `status`, `size`, `created_at_ms`, `sidecar_path`, `sidecar_sha256` | **cleartext** |
| `parent_folder_ipns_name`, `child_ipns_name`, `file_meta_ipns_name` | **cleartext** (routing keys) |
| `filename_encrypted_hex` / `name_encrypted_hex` | hex(ECIES-wrapped-to-user-EC-pubkey) |
| `wrapped_key_hex`, `parent_ipns_key_hex`, `child_ipns_key_hex`, `file_ipns_key_hex`, `child_folder_key_hex` | hex(ECIES-wrapped) |
| `iv_hex` | cleartext |
| content | separate `.bin`, AES-256-GCM ciphertext only |

Doc invariant at the top of the file: *"The journal stores only ciphertext + ECIES-wrapped keys — never plaintext or raw key bytes (zero-knowledge constraint, D-05)."* Tests enforcing it: `journal_no_plaintext`, `journal_no_plaintext_filename`, `sidecar_ciphertext_not_in_json`.

v1's staging bytes also weren't only in the journal: `v1:crates/fuse/src/file_handle.rs` (`OpenFileHandle`) buffers every writable open into an **untracked, unbudgeted** temp file (zeroed before deletion, but never counted). That's a second disk consumer v2's budget policy needs to account for if `FileStagingStore` subsumes it.

---

## 3. Desktop local journal — v1 original of `FileStagingStore`

- **Location:** `default_journal_dir()` in `v1:apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/fuse/mod.rs:66` → `dirs::data_local_dir()/cipherbox/cb-journal`, with a `std::env::temp_dir()` fallback (which logs *"may not survive reboot"*). `create_dir_all` + `0o700` at mount.
- **Single shared directory for all vaults and all accounts** — scoping is the read-time `vault_root_ipns` filter only.
- **Two constructors, one path, by design (CR-07):** the FUSE mount (`fuse/mod.rs:163`) and the sync daemon (`commands/sync.rs:59`) each build their own `WriteQueue` over the same dir, both using `JOURNAL_MAX_RETRIES`. There is no shared handle and no lock — coherence is "the filesystem is the database".
- **Ordering at mount** (`fuse/mod.rs` ~200-240): GC first (synchronous, best-effort), then `replay_for_vault` spawned **concurrently with** the mount, never blocking it. *"Errors are logged but never fail the mount — a partially-replayed journal is better than a failed mount."*
- **The daemon is a pure observer.** `v1:crates/sdk/src/sync.rs` (30s `SYNC_INTERVAL`) calls `load_all_for_vault` each cycle, counts `Pending` vs `Failed`, and emits `SyncStatus::WriteParked { pending, failed }` → tray `TrayStatus::WriteParked` ("Upload Failed"). It **never drains** the queue; only mount-time replay does. Parked writes are therefore invisible until the next mount, and the daemon must be running or the user never learns (G-43-UAT-01).

---

1. **`sealed(op)` is stronger than v1.** v1 leaks, in cleartext, per-op: which vault, which parent folder IPNS name, file size, and timing. Sealing the whole op fixes that — but v1 depends on `vault_root_ipns` and `status`/`created_at_ms` being readable *without keys* for `load_all_for_vault`, `gc_failed_entries`, and the daemon's `WriteParked` count. If v2 seals the op body, keep owner_tag **and** authored_at **and** a coarse status/size outside the seal, or accept that GC and status reporting require an unlocked vault.
2. **Foreign-entry handling should be tiered, not binary.** v1 distinguishes *foreign* (skip silently), *malformed* (skip + warn), *schema-drift* (migrate via serde alias/default, one-time passthrough, never re-persist the legacy shape), and *corrupt payload* (retain + retry + eventually park). v2's "undecodable → ?" needs at minimum the corrupt-vs-legacy split; conflating them either destroys writes or publishes garbage. `decrypt_journal_name` is the canonical example.
3. **Parked entries need a GC or they are a DoS.** v1 keeps `Failed` on disk forever for manual recovery, which required adding a 30-day / 500 MiB oldest-first sweep (T-52-16). If v2's staging store retains failures, budget for it explicitly.
4. **Never trust a path stored inside the record.** Re-derive it from the record id.
5. **Purge on logout / account switch.** v1 only wired `purge_vault` at `logout()` and flagged `switch_account` / `delete_account` as an outstanding caller.
6. **v1's op vocabulary was only `UploadFile` + `MkdirPublish`.** Deletes, renames, and per-file/bin IPNS publishes were explicitly *not* journaled — `publish_with_cas_retry` carries a dead `journal_entry: Option<()>` parameter documented as "always None this phase" precisely because no `JournalOp::FilePublish` variant existed. # Ship

Take the current feature branch through the full ship loop **autonomously, without babysitting**:
verify → security review → simplify → local test gates → CodeRabbit CLI → PR → resolve reviews → green.

Scope: the current branch's diff against `origin/main` — one PR-sized slice of blueprint work. `branch feat/settings-name-kdf-edge in worktree .claude/worktrees/agent-ab4ecfb6720a3153e — issue #861, core: settings-name KDF edge and regenerated catalog KATs` may name a branch or PR number; if empty, use the checked-out branch.

## Operating rules (so this needs no babysitting)

- **Decide, don't ask.** For every review/audit finding, pick exactly one of **three** dispositions and proceed. The default for anything that isn't clearly material is **discard**, not defer — the issue backlog is a signal for real upcoming work, so keep it small.
  - **Fix now** — the finding is a genuine bug, security/privacy issue, or correctness gap **AND** (it's in the slice's domain OR the fix is small and safe). Always fix real defects the slice itself introduced, regardless of size, or block on them if you can't.
  - **File an issue** — defer via `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh issue create` **only if the item clears the materiality bar**: it's a real defect or a concrete, actionable piece of future work, that you are choosing not to do now because it's out of domain, risky, or large. Before filing, **search open issues and dedupe** — comment on a near-duplicate rather than opening a new one. Reference filed issues in the PR.
  - **Discard** — do nothing and do not file. This is the right call for: style/naming/formatting nits, subjective preferences, speculative "could hypothetically" findings with no demonstrated impact, micro-optimizations, test-only suggestions of marginal value, and low-severity **pre-existing** noise unrelated to the slice. Briefly acknowledge dismissed classes in the PR (e.g. "N nits dismissed") rather than filing them.
  - **Materiality bar for an issue** (must meet at least one): user-visible or data-integrity impact; security/privacy/crypto relevance; a real crash/correctness risk; or a concrete follow-up the build will genuinely need. "A reviewer mentioned it" is not sufficient. When unsure whether an item clears the bar, **discard it**.
  - Only stop for: a real failing gate you cannot fix, a genuine ambiguity in intent, or the final merge decision.
- **Verify outcomes faithfully.** Quote real test output. Never report a step done that wasn't.
- Run independent checks in parallel. Keep yourself as orchestrator; hand large self-contained chunks to sub-agents (Rust builds, mechanical sweeps) and adversarially verify their results.
- The blueprint corpus (`blueprint/*.md`, `CONTEXT.md`) is normative — a finding that contradicts it is judged against the blueprint, not reviewer preference.

## Environment gotchas (apply throughout)

- Prefix every GitHub CLI call with `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh …`.
- **`git push` / `git fetch` are blocked in the sandbox in this environment** — run them with the sandbox disabled. Plain `gh api` reads/writes work sandboxed.
- Commit signing goes through the 1Password SSH agent: **guard every commit with `timeout`** — a hung signer wedges 1Password (the fix is restarting the app, not retrying). Never `--no-gpg-sign` unless the user says so. If a commit errors or times out, **verify with `git log --oneline -1` before retrying** — it may have landed.
- `gh pr edit` fails on this repo (Projects-classic GraphQL) — patch the body via `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file`.
- PR title + commit subjects: **conventional, no parentheses in the subject** (commitlint + `lint-pr-title` CI reject parens). Escape bare `#NN` item refs as `` `#NN` `` in PR bodies (GFM autolinks them).
- `markdownlint --fix` + prettier run on staged `.md` at commit — headings not bold, blank lines around fences/lists/tables.

## Steps

### 1. Verify

Invoke `/verify`: drive the affected flow end-to-end against the real app/stack — not just tests or typecheck. Fix real gaps; re-run until the behavior is observed working.

### 2. Security review

Invoke `/security-review` on the slice diff (`origin/main...HEAD`) — a general vulnerability sweep (injection, authz, secrets, unsafe deserialization, etc.). Triage each finding with the three-way operating rule.

### 2b. Crypto/privacy review (conditional)

**Only when the slice touched crypto- or privacy-adjacent code.** Check the diff for the signal before deciding:

```bash
git diff origin/main...HEAD --name-only | grep -iE 'crypt|cipher|seal|unseal|kdf|derive|epoch|grant|hpke|xchacha|blake3|ed25519|secp256k1|key|ipns|nonce|zeroiz|pointer|floor|adoption|privacy' | grep -vE '\.test\.|__tests__|/tests/|\.md$'
```

If that surfaces nothing relevant, **skip this step** and note "no crypto/privacy-adjacent changes" in the PR. Otherwise invoke `/crypto-privacy-review` scoped to the changed files, judge findings against `blueprint/core.md` and `CONTEXT.md` (the KDF edge catalog, structure tags, adoption gate, and floor law are normative), triage three-way, and summarize the outcome in the PR body.

### 3. Simplify

Invoke `/simplify` on the slice diff — reuse, duplication, dead code, altitude. Apply safe simplifications; file an issue for a larger refactor only if it clears the materiality bar, otherwise discard.

### 4. Local test gates — DO NOT SKIP

Run the PR-gate suites for the touched area locally before pushing (`blueprint/testing.md` owns the suite map):

- **cargo workspace tests** — core KATs + property layer, engine simulation scenarios — whenever `crates/*` changed.
- **`packages/client` browser suite** — whenever the WASM boundary, seams, or leadership code changed.
- **The contract suite** — the **only** live client→API integration gate (the sdk-e2e descendant; its v1 ancestor caught a 48/89 break unit suites missed). Run it whenever the slice touched the API surface, the engine's API client, the registry/publish path, or key lifecycle. Needs the CI stack up: postgres, Kubo, the API under test, and the local `/routing/v1` record store (`tools/mock-ipns-routing`).

Transitional note: while v2 suites are still landing, run whatever `ci.yml` currently gates for the touched paths. Must be all green — quote the real output.

### 5. CodeRabbit CLI review (local, before ship)

```bash
coderabbit review --agent --base main --type committed
```

Triage every finding with the three-way operating rule. Re-run until the in-scope set is clean. (The CLI under-reports vs the web review — for crypto/durability-heavy slices, request a full web review on the PR as well.)

### 6. Ship

- **Create the PR as a DRAFT** (`env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh pr create --draft ...`) with a conventional, paren-free title. Drafting defers CodeRabbit's PR review until the branch is settled — mark ready only when you're done pushing.
- Write the PR body to a temp file (escape `#NN`; **no** Claude session link or "Generated with Claude Code" footer) and set it at create time or via `gh api -X PATCH`.
- Push with the sandbox disabled.
- When the branch is settled: `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh pr ready <N>`.

### 7. Resolve PR reviews

When CodeRabbit's PR-level review lands (poll `gh pr checks <N>` in the background until the `CodeRabbit` check is no longer pending — don't block):

- CodeRabbit bundles findings in the **review body** AND as inline **review threads**. Fetch threads via the GraphQL `reviewThreads` query (id, isResolved, path, line, first comment body). Query **all** threads, no author filter — Greptile reviews too, sometimes late; CodeRabbit's author is `coderabbitai`, not `coderabbitai[bot]`. Expect re-reviews of your own fix commits — triage those too.
- For each finding apply the three-way operating rule (fix → reference the commit; material defer → reference the issue; nit → resolve the thread with a brief "acknowledged, not actionable" reply, nothing filed).
- Then run `/resolve-pr-reviews`, or directly: reply to each thread (`addPullRequestReviewThreadReply`) with the disposition and resolve it (`resolveReviewThread`). GitHub's API is occasionally flaky — wrap mutations in a small retry loop and re-query `reviewThreads` afterward to confirm **0 unresolved** and no duplicate replies.

### 8. Confirm green & report

Poll `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh pr checks <N>` until all checks settle. Report: final commit SHA, CI status (all green / which failed), threads resolved (`N/N`), a triage tally (fixed / issues filed / discarded), and the list of issues filed. Keep the filed count low — if it's climbing, re-check that each cleared the materiality bar. Leave the merge decision to the user.

content.content:
Adds the fifteenth KDF edge so the vault settings record has a network-resolvable name that needs no CipherBox infrastructure. Settled by #825 on wayfinder map #813, overturning #822's `PUT/GET /account/settings`.

## Why

`AGENTS.md` commits to the network being canonical and CipherBox infra being accelerator-only. Holding a self-hosting user's own node config on the API is circular: they would need CipherBox to tell them where their own node is. v1 got this right — `apps/web/src/services/vault-settings.service.ts` on branch `v1` publishes settings under a dedicated derived IPNS name (`deriveVaultSettingsIpnsKeypair`) with no server surface at all.

## Scope

- A fifteenth edge in the frozen catalog (`crates/core/src/kdf/mod.rs`): name `settings-ipns-keypair`, context `cipherbox/v2/settings-ipns-keypair`, input layout `ed25519_from_seed(derive_key(ctx, loginSecret[var]))` — mirroring v1's derive-from-user-key shape and `vault-pointer-index`'s existing `loginSecret` origin.
- `EDGES` grows to fifteen; the module doc's "fourteen edges" claim updates with it.
- `edge_probe_outputs` gains its row, in catalog order.
- Regenerate the KAT manifest and the mechanical cross-edge separation vector (no two edges share an output for equal inputs).

Only **one** new edge is needed: the settings payload seals HPKE-to-self under the existing `enc-subkey`, which is v2's analogue of v1's ECIES-to-own-public-key and is already the precedent for the owner write blob, #818's content key and #832's op body. It is `loginSecret`-derived, so it is available at cold start before any resolve.

## Gate

`Core KATs (native + WASM)` — including the existing freshness step, which fails closed if the committed vectors are not regenerated.

## Dependencies

None. Startable immediately, in parallel with the whole engine chain.

Part of #655

### 1. Domain separation — PASS

- `cipherbox/v2/settings-ipns-keypair` is correctly `cipherbox/v2/<edge>`-shaped and unique. `edge_contexts_are_unique_and_v2_prefixed` (`crates/core/src/kdf/mod.rs:514`) mechanically enforces both the uniqueness and the `format!("cipherbox/v2/{name}")` equality, so the string cannot drift from the name.
- Collision with the other `loginSecret` edges is infeasible. `enc-subkey`, `owner-pointer-seed` and the new edge are all `blake3::derive_key(ctx, secret)` with distinct contexts — BLAKE3 `derive_key` mixes the context through a separate key-derivation-context flag/chaining value, so equal output across two contexts is a BLAKE3 collision.
- **The `vault-pointer-index` asymmetry is safe and intentional.** `vault-pointer-index` is `keyed_hash(derive_key(ctx_vpi, secret), index[8 BE])`; the new edge is a bare `derive_key(ctx_s, secret)`. They differ in *both* the context string and the BLAKE3 mode (keyed-hash flag vs derive-key-material flag), so there is no shape under which one can be reached from the other. The extra `keyed_hash` layer exists purely because `vault-pointer-index` has an index dimension; the settings name has none, so adding a constant-message `keyed_hash` would be ceremonial, not security-bearing. This also matches `owner-pointer-seed`, the existing bare-`derive_key` loginSecret edge.
- Confusion is further prevented at the type level: the settings edge returns `Ed25519Signer`, `enc-subkey` returns `X25519Secret`, `owner-pointer-seed` returns `SecretBytes`.
- Cross-edge separation is asserted three ways for the new row automatically: the in-crate `edges_are_pairwise_separated` (`kdf/mod.rs:501`), the frozen-vector set-cardinality check (`kat_manifest.rs`), and the proptest over arbitrary inputs (`crates/core/tests/kdf_props.rs:38`).

### 2. Catalog freeze integrity — PASS, verified

`git diff origin/main...HEAD --numstat -- crates/core/kat/` is `6 1` on `manifest.json` and `6 0` on `vectors/kdf/edges.json`. The single deleted line in `manifest.json` is `"count": 14` → `15`. **Zero pre-existing frozen outputs changed** — every other KAT vector file is untouched by the diff. I ran `cargo test -p cipherbox-core kdf`: `kdf_catalog_freezes_names_contexts_and_layouts` and `kdf_edge_outputs_are_frozen_and_pairwise_separated` both pass, i.e. the committed vectors are recomputed byte-for-byte from the current implementation. The CI freshness gate (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:432`, `cargo run --example kat_gen` + `git diff --exit-code -- crates/core/kat`) remains the backstop.

### 3. Secret handling — PASS

`settings_ipns_keypair_bytes` (`crates/core/src/kdf/mod.rs:230`) returns `SecretBytes`, which zeroizes on drop and has a redacted `Debug`. No new logging, no `Debug`/`Display` on secret material, no serialization of the seed. `EdgeProbeOutput`'s `Debug` is already redacted and the new row inherits it. The function is pure — the caller-owned `login_secret: &[u8]` is only read, never zeroed by the callee, which is exactly the repo's terminal-owner rule.

### 4. Privacy — acceptable, matches v1 and the existing pointer-name class

- The `ipnsName` is `Ed25519(BLAKE3-derive_key(ctx, loginSecret))`. One-wayness means publishing it leaks **nothing** about the login secret.
- **No cryptographic linkage to the user's other names.** Given the settings name, deriving `vault-pointer-index(secret, i)` or the scope-pointer names requires the login secret; the names are mutually unguessable (256-bit). The 15 edges' outputs are pairwise independent under the separation law.
- What is observably leaked to anyone who *already knows* the name: existence, publish cadence (IPNS sequence numbers + validity/EOL timestamps), and the ciphertext length of the settings blob. - Linkage across a user's names is possible only out-of-band (same publishing peer/IP/time window, or via the API republisher, which already knows the account). This is the pre-existing model, unchanged by this edge.

Comment on the existing issue, do not open a new one.

**2. The settings name is unrotatable by construction.** Unlike `vault-pointer-index`, which carries an `index[8 BE]` re-point chain so an owner-plane name can be moved, this edge is a pure function of the login secret with no index or epoch input. Reasoning to include, so a human reviewer can overrule with full information: (a) #861's layout was settled by #825 on wayfinder map #813, explicitly overturning #822, so filing would re-litigate a decided design; (b) the compromise scenario is not an incremental exposure — the settings signer is derived from `loginSecret`, and so are `enc-subkey` and `owner-pointer-seed`, so any leak that exposes this signer implies `loginSecret` compromise, which is already game-over; (c) it intentionally mirrors v1's `deriveVaultSettingsIpnsKeypair`. Ship worker for #863 is running. Beyond the standard gates I pointed it at the slice's real risk areas rather than letting it review generically:

- Whether the `Option<u64>` "unprojected ≠ zero" distinction holds on *every* path, or a `None` can silently render as 0
- The `record_sequence` question the implementing agent raised — it isn't carried forward and resets to 1 on re-projection. I told the worker to actually determine whether the conditional-delete rebase depends on it surviving a root advance, and to fix it if so rather than accept the agent's "left it alone to avoid widening scope"
- Fail-closed behavior of the wasm/TS boundary mapper on an unknown pending value
- `/crypto-privacy-review` is mandatory here — `net/resolve.rs` is the gated resolve path, which is adoption-gate and floor-law territory

Board:

| | State |
|---|---|
| #861 | ship worker — 3 gates clean, findings forwarded, heading to PR |
| #863 | ship worker — gates running, targeted to merge first |
| #862 | still building |
| #864 | still building, scope grew by #863's deferred bullet 4 |

Once #864 lands I'll do a real test-merge against #863 rather than relying on my predicted conflict, and I'll check #862's file set for any third-way overlap.

**#861 is shipped and green — PR #874, ready for review, `MERGEABLE`.**

https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box/pull/874 — final commit `4c9a74016`.

I verified independently rather than taking the report at face value: 14 checks pass, 0 fail (the rest correctly `skipping` on path filters). The named gate `Core KATs (native + WASM)` passes at 4m30s. PR is out of draft.

**Triage: 3 fixed, 0 issues filed, 8 discarded, 1 comment on #870.**

The one genuine defect the slice introduced was caught by the crypto review — `crates/core/src/suite/ed25519.rs` enumerated four Ed25519-seed edges and this slice made a fifth. The worker replaced the list with a `crate::kdf` cross-reference rather than appending a name, so it can't rot again on the next edge. It also added the missing **Vault settings record** term to `CONTEXT.md`, which the diff had introduced as a domain noun in two files without defining.

Two things worth your attention on the merge decision:

**The settings name is unrotatable by construction** — no index or epoch dimension, unlike `vault-pointer-index`. Both the security and crypto reviewers independently raised it; both concluded discard, and I agree: the layout was settled by #825 on #813, any leak exposing this signer implies `loginSecret` compromise anyway, and the remedy if ever needed is another additive edge — the frozen catalog doesn't foreclose it. It's a visible section in the PR body with the counterpoint stated, not buried, so you can overrule.

**`kdf::settings_ipns_keypair` is intentionally dead public API** in this slice; #870 is the consumer and lists this edge as a blocker.

One incidental finding: **Greptile appears inactive on this repo** — no reviews on #874 or on recent PRs #848, #847, #840. That's a change from the two-reviewer assumption I'd been working under, so CodeRabbit is currently the only bot gate.

Still running: **#863** ship (targeted to merge before #864), **#862** and **#864** implementations.

The merge source is the **base** cell, never the rendered view. Non-adopting verdicts are untouched: `TrustViolation`/`Current`/`NoUpdate` still return `false` and leave last-known-good whole (`crates/engine/src/net/resolve.rs:347-354`), which is what `blueprint/engine.md:163` requires. Keying the merge on `NodeId` and letting `ipnsName` change underneath is therefore *required* for correctness, not a hazard.

The adversarial case does not cross a trust boundary: only the owner or a write-grantee holding the scope's write seed can author a root body, and `assert_children_unique` (`crates/core/src/seal/body.rs:272,314`) already binds id/ipnsName uniqueness. The merge source is the **base** cell, never the rendered view. All three are gate-derived; `apply_overlay` clones and never mutates the base. So every carried value was itself produced by a prior gate pass — the merge cannot smuggle overlay/unverified state across a verdict.

Non-adopting verdicts are untouched: `TrustViolation`/`Current`/`NoUpdate` still return `false` and leave last-known-good whole (`crates/engine/src/net/resolve.rs:347-354`), which is what `blueprint/engine.md:163` requires. content.text:
**#862 landed** — branch `feat/engine-content-format-kat`, commit `f65521162`.

**My flagged KAT-manifest conflict did not materialize**, and I was wrong about the mechanism: #862 created a *separate* `crates/engine/kat/` tree rather than extending core's manifest, so it never touches #861's files. Good outcome, wrong prediction on my part.

I then verified the merge interactions empirically instead of reasoning about them:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| #862 → post-#861 `main` | clean |
| #863 → post-#861 `main` | clean |
| #863 then #862 sequentially | clean (textual) |
| Combined tree `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` | **exit 0** |
| Combined tree `cargo test --workspace` | **826 passed, 0 failed** |
| Engine KAT freshness on combined | no drift |
| Core KAT freshness on combined | no drift |

That matters because #862 and #863 both edit `crates/engine/src/facade.rs` and `crates/wasm/src/host.rs` — textually clean but semantically independent, now confirmed by a real build rather than a green mergeability badge. Temp worktree cleaned up.

**The substantive find in #862:** `assemble` didn't validate leaf-CID well-formedness while `decode_root` hard-rejects it — a live violation of the repo's encode/decode fail-closed rule, meaning a mis-wired caller could publish a root the crate's own decoder refuses. Now a release-active `Err(MalformedLeafCid)` with a test that fires in release builds. It also found the pre-existing `dummy_leaves` test helper was generating all-zero invalid CIDs.

Frozen: `chunk_size = 1_048_536` (+40 B seal overhead = exactly 1 MiB), `ROOT_FORMAT_VERSION = 1`, flat-DAG ceiling 110,375 links = 107.78 GiB — matching #820's stated figure. 10 vectors, 5 accept / 5 reject.

**Two things I'm carrying forward, not silently accepting:**

1. #862's self-review was an *internal* pass. `/simplify`, `/security-review`, and `/crypto-privacy-review` still owe a run against the real PR diff — I'll enforce that in its ship, not treat the agent's self-check as satisfying the mandatory gates.
2. It deliberately scoped the check sweep to `DagError`, leaving ~10 other engine error types with `check()` but no `CHECKS` const (adoption gate, grants, rotation). That's a real follow-up needing a dependency edge back to #820 — I'll file it with the edge when #862 ships, rather than let it evaporate.

**#864 is the last one still building.** Once it reports I'll rerun this same combined-build check with all three, since it rewrites `sync/op.rs` where #863 added `Op::pending_class()` — the one collision I still expect to be real.

Resume and finish PR #875. Important: you ended your turn saying you were "standing by" for the CodeRabbit cooldown — that does not work here. Ending a turn to wait is a silent lost-wake: nothing resumes you, and the review would never have been processed. You only run while a turn is active. This is a known recurring failure mode in this repo, so treat it as a hard rule: **never end a turn intending to come back to something.**

Wait for the cooldown **inline, in the foreground, within this single turn**. The Bash tool caps at 600000 ms (10 minutes) per call, so chain several sequential foreground calls in the same turn — e.g. `sleep 540` repeatedly — polling between each. Budget up to ~45 minutes total. Do not background the wait, do not use a detached sleep, and do not stop until you have either processed the review or exhausted the budget.

Poll between sleeps with:
```
env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/875/reviews --jq '.[] | {user:.user.login, state:.state, submitted:.submitted_at}'
env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh pr checks 875
```

Context on why the wait exists: CodeRabbit's web review is **automatic on PR-ready and rate-limited to roughly one per hour org-wide**. PR #874 was reviewed and merged shortly before yours, which is what consumed the quota. So do **not** manually request a review — that is explicitly discouraged in this repo and wastes quota. Just wait for the automatic one.

When it lands:
- Confirm it is a real **review pass**, not just a walkthrough — look for "Actionable comments posted: N". A walkthrough alone means it has not actually reviewed.
- Fetch **all** review threads via the GraphQL `reviewThreads` query with **no author filter**. CodeRabbit's author is `coderabbitai`, not `coderabbitai[bot]`. Note for your expectations: Greptile appears inactive on this repo right now — it left no review on #874 or on recent PRs #848/#847/#840 — so CodeRabbit is likely the only bot reviewer. - Your `record_sequence` verdict was well-argued and I accept it — particularly the point that conditional delete is *already* inert on `main` so this slice changes nothing, and your rejection of the `ipns_name` equality gate because a write rotation legitimately changes `ipnsName` for a stable `id16`. impl StoragePolicy { pub fn measured(StoragePlatform, headroom_bytes: u64) -> Self; pub const CI: Self }

Folded in: ephemeral scalar and encoded op body now zeroize at the terminal owner (the recipient pubkey is in the clear header, so the scalar alone reopens the body); `stage_op` now `verify_cid`s the staged bytes against the root CID; the op-record KAT family; a trimmed over-claiming dead-letter comment.

**Deliberately left out — flagging for your call:**
1. **`OP_RECORD_V` is bound into the AAD but not carried in the clear header.** A future format bump would make every queued record fail to open → `Undecodable` → dead-lettered and removed, silently deleting a user's offline queue, with no way to tell version skew from corruption. 5. **Missing `navigator.storage.estimate()` yields a zero budget**, i.e. no uploads. That is #829's honest-no-floor-up rule, and content uploads are still `Unimplemented`, but it conflates "measured tiny" with "could not measure".
6. **The owner tag is a raw long-term X25519 public key at rest**, unencrypted per origin — a local linkability surface. #832 §2 settled "verbatim, no derivation, no hash", so unchanged.

v1 recon (mandatory): v1's `crates/sdk/src/queue.rs` `JournalEntry` corroborates both settled decisions — it carried a cleartext `vault_root_ipns` owner tag and silently skipped foreign entries, and its per-op `created_at_ms` became the published mtime (authored, not replay time). v1 has **no** storage-headroom policy at all, so nothing there contradicts the `min(CAP, FRACTION x (headroom − ceiling))` formula. content.text:
What would you like to clarify?

For context, here's the shape of the decision in case it helps sharpen the question:

**The mechanism.** `crates/core/src/seal/op_record.rs` seals with `OP_RECORD_V` mixed into the AAD, but the clear header is only `{owner_tag, content_root_cid}`. HPKE binds the version, so if the version ever changes, every already-queued record fails its authentication tag. The engine can't tell "wrong version" from "corrupt bytes" — both land in `RecordClass::Undecodable`, and the cold-start path dead-letters and removes those. So a future format bump silently deletes any user's pending offline op queue.

**Why it's a decision and not just a fix.** #832 §3 settles the record as exactly three parts. Adding a cleartext `v` overturns that. I don't have the reasoning behind §3 in front of me, and unilaterally reversing a settled spec is not a call I should make.

**Why timing matters.** The format is unpublished and unfrozen right now. #865–#872 build directly on this record, so the same change becomes a breaking wire-format migration shortly.

Things you might be probing at that I can go find out rather than have you adjudicate blind:

- What #832 §3 actually argues — I can pull the issue and quote its reasoning on the three-part shape
- Whether #819/#824 already scope a retained/held record class, and how far along that thinking is
- Whether the version can be recovered some other way — e.g. trial-decrypting against known versions, which would make the clear `v` unnecessary
- Whether anything else in the codebase already survives a format bump, so there's an established pattern to follow

Happy to dig into any of those first, or just answer whatever you're actually asking.

content.content:
Part of #813

## Question

What happens to a non-empty durable op queue across logout and an account switch on the same device?

## Why it is now specifiable

Surfaced while resolving #818. That decision seals the staged content key to the owner's `enc-subkey`, so a foreign identity meeting another account's queued ops now fails **closed** — but only for the key. What the engine should *do* with an alien or abandoned queue is untouched.

## The gap

- The staging store is namespaced per origin, not per account (`packages/client/src/worker/browserSeams.ts:22` — `dbPrefix` "namespaces per origin/test"). Two accounts on one browser profile share one op queue and one staged-bytes directory.
- `StagingStore` has **no `clear`** (`crates/engine/src/seams/staging_store.rs:24-51`), unlike `SnapshotCache::clear`, whose contents "survive logout by design" and are cleared only by an explicit forget-this-device (`seams/snapshot_cache.rs:15-17`). Nothing states whether the op queue inherits that survive-logout default or the opposite.
- The ops themselves are opaque bytes to the store, and carry no identity — only a target `NodeId` and a base sequence (`sync/op.rs:20-32`). Nothing in a queued op says whose it is.

So today: user A queues an offline upload, logs out, user B logs in on the same profile. B's engine sees A's ops in the queue. Under #818 the content key will not open, so the content op dead-letters — but a `Rename` or `Delete` op carries no sealed material at all and would be replayed against B's tree.

## What to establish

1. Whether logout clears the op queue, preserves it, or preserves it under an identity-scoped namespace.
2. If preserved: what a returning user sees, and what the drain does with ops formed against a tree the device no longer has.
3. Whether a queued op needs an identity binding so a foreign queue is detectable for *all* op kinds, not only the content ones #818 happens to protect.
4. Where the staged bytes go — they are budget-consuming and are the one thing that cannot be re-derived.

## Context

#862 froze the content format and landed the first engine-side KAT, but scoped its
fail-closed **check sweep** to `DagError` only. #820 §5 records that *every* engine
fail-closed check is unswept — the content plane is one of eleven.

After #862, `crates/engine/src/content/dag.rs` is the only engine error type carrying a
`CHECKS` const, a `check()` that is pinned against it in declaration order, and a reject
vector per check. The other ten have a `check()` string surface with nothing pinning it:
add a variant, forget its `check()` arm or its vector, and nothing fails.

## The ten unswept surfaces

Adoption gate:

- `GateRejection` — `crates/engine/src/gate/adoption.rs`

Grants plane:

- `CreateGrantError` — `crates/engine/src/grants/create.rs`
- `AuthorityViolation` — `crates/engine/src/grants/ledger.rs`
- `AbuseEvent` — `crates/engine/src/grants/owner_entry.rs`

Rotation plane:

- `CascadeError` — `crates/engine/src/rotation/cascade.rs`
- `ResealError` — `crates/engine/src/rotation/reseal.rs`
- `WriteRotateError` — `crates/engine/src/rotation/rotate_write.rs`
- `RotateError` — `crates/engine/src/rotation/rotate.rs`
- `SweepError` — `crates/engine/src/rotation/sweep.rs`
- `RevokeError` — `crates/engine/src/rotation/trigger.rs`

## Scope

Per plane, mirroring the shape #862 established for `DagError`:

1. A `CHECKS: &'static [&'static str]` const in declaration order, with a prefix that
   cannot collide with a core check or another engine plane's, plus the
   `the_check_surface_matches_the_variants_in_order` test that makes a new variant
   without a check name a compile-or-test failure.
2. A `class()` that is exhaustive over the variants, so a new variant must state whether
   it is a trust verdict, an availability outcome, or a client-capability limit rather
   than inheriting `"trust"` — the misclassification #862 fixed for
   `UnsupportedFormat`.
3. A reject-vector family per plane emitted by a committed generator, on the
   `crates/engine/examples/kat_gen.rs` + `crates/engine/kat/**` pattern, with the
   `Engine Tests` freshness step extended to cover it.

This is a cross-plane slice — three vector families, three generators' worth of fixture
construction against the rotation and grants planes — which is why it was not folded
into #862.

## Gate

`Engine Tests`: the extended freshness step plus the per-plane sweep tests, each
blocking on the day it lands.

## Dependencies

- Depends on #635 (engine: implement rotation primitives, sweep, name wave, and grants) —
  the rotation and grants planes must be feature-complete before their reject vectors are
  worth freezing, or the vectors churn every slice.
- Related: #812 (encode-side fail-closed guards for the child read-path rejects) — the
  encode/decode symmetry half of the same AGENTS.md rule 8 debt; disjoint work, same law.

Found by the ship-flow review gates on the #862 PR.

Part of #655

The freeze is definitional until the upload path lands, which makes this KAT the only thing exercising production framing today. Correct for this issue's scope, worth knowing when the upload slice arrives.</result>

**#876 is now wired into tracking.** It had *zero* native edges — the prose "## Dependencies" section was there, but nothing machine-readable, so nothing would have picked it up.

**Dependency edges (GitHub native, the mechanism this repo actually uses):**

```
#876 blocked_by → #635  (rotation primitives, sweep, name wave, grants)
#876 blocked_by → #862  (freeze content format + engine KAT)
```

Verified the reverse direction resolved automatically: `#635 blocking → 876`, `#862 blocking → 868,876`. That matches the existing convention (`#868 <- 867,862`).

I used `blocked_by` only for the two hard blockers. **#812 I left as prose** — the issue calls it "Related: … disjoint work, same law," and GitHub's native dependencies only express blocking, so encoding a non-blocking relationship there would have falsely blocked #876.

**Added to tracker #655**, placed at the end of the write-plane block after #872, since it descends from #862 and sits after both blockers in build order.

**And an audit turned up three stale checkboxes.** I checked all 55 tracker entries against real issue state rather than just adding my line:

| Issue | Was | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| #633 grants ledger, contact import, mailbox | `[ ]` | CLOSED |
| #640 tab leadership, broadcast, leader failover | `[ ]` | CLOSED |
| #644 desktop hardware verification gates | `[ ]` | CLOSED |

All three now ticked. Worth knowing because **#633 being closed changes what I told you earlier** — I said the grants trio in #876 was "ambiguous" partly on the assumption #633 was open. The grants ledger is in fact done; only #635 still gates that plane.

That does not unblock #876 overall — #635 is still open, and #862 is still in ship. But the edges now mean the tracker will surface #876 the moment both clear, without anyone remembering it exists.

<result>## SIMPLIFY review — no files modified

Diff: `origin/main...HEAD` (2 commits, 41 files, +2616/−318). Ranked by value.

---

### 1. `crates/engine/src/sync/authored.rs` (whole new file, 70 lines) — a module for one 4-line function with one caller

`stamp_authored` has exactly one production caller: `overlay.rs` (4 call sites in the same `match`). The header justifies the split by a component that does not exist:

> "the one place the pending-op overlay **and the drain's publish plan** both read from"

`grep -rn drain crates/engine/src` finds no drain module — only test helpers named `drain()` and four forward-references to this imaginary one (`authored.rs:2`, `overlay.rs:29`, `op.rs:217`, `staging.rs:83,331`). That is a module, a `pub` export, a `pub use` in `sync/mod.rs:50`, a re-export in `lib.rs:94`, a 3-line module doc, and 3 tests, all created to serve a future second caller. This is exactly the shape `#853` bans.

**Fix:** delete `authored.rs`; move the 4 lines into `overlay.rs` as a private `fn stamp_authored(meta: &mut NodeMeta, op: &Op)`; drop both re-exports. Fold the 3 tests into `overlay.rs`'s existing test module (two of them — `a_metadata_op_stamps_its_authored_time_and_leaves_size_alone` and `a_projected_mtime_is_overwritten_never_merely_filled` — assert the same thing twice; keep the second).

### 2. `crates/engine/src/storage_policy.rs:25-28,44-53,78-80,92-98,107,115` — the read-cache half of the policy has zero consumers

`read_cache_ceiling_bytes`, `cache_cap_bytes`, and `cache_percent` are computed, stored, exported, and asserted in 6 tests. **No production code reads any of them** — the sealed-block read cache does not exist yet. `StoragePlatform::DESKTOP` (`:48-53`) is referenced only by this file's own unit tests; the desktop shell never constructs an engine with it.

This isn't free dead weight: the cache reservation is subtracted from headroom *before* the staging fraction (`:92-94`), so it materially changes the only budget that is enforced, on the basis of a ceiling nothing enforces. It also drags in the 5-line Storage Standard §7 module paragraph (`:9-13`) and 3 tests (`the_cache_reservation_comes_off_headroom_before_the_staging_fraction`, plus the cache halves of `a_generous_headroom_lands_on_the_platform_cap` and `a_headroom_near_the_integer_ceiling_does_not_wrap`).

**Fix:** cut the cache fields and `DESKTOP` until the read cache and the desktop wiring land. `measured` becomes:

```rust
pub fn measured(platform: StoragePlatform, headroom_bytes: u64) -> Self {
    Self {
        staging_budget_bytes: percent_of(headroom_bytes, platform.staging_percent)
            .min(platform.staging_cap_bytes),
        headroom: Headroom::Measured,
    }
}
```

Net: ~70 lines gone, including the module header paragraph and 3 test bodies.

### 3. `crates/engine/src/sync/record.rs:122-136` — `RetainedReason`'s two variants are never distinguished by any consumer

Both variants are *constructed* (`:94`, `:97`), neither is ever *read*. Every production consumer discards the payload: `rebase.rs` does `RecordClass::Retained(_) => scan.retained += 1`, `facade.rs` counts. The only code that inspects the reason is `record.rs`'s own two unit tests.

Worse, the doc comments promise a distinction the data model cannot deliver. `facade.rs:168-172` claims a host reports *"this device holds work from another account **or** a newer version"* — but `retained_records: usize` is a single count with no reason attached, so the host literally cannot say which.

**Fix, pick one:** (a) drop the payload — `Retained` with no data; the two tests still prove "retained, not undecodable", which is the behaviour that matters. Or (b) if the host really must distinguish, carry it: `QueueScan { retained_foreign: usize, retained_forward: usize }` and thread it to `SnapshotView`. Do not ship (c) — the current state, where the enum exists solely so a comment can claim a capability. Same defect on `RecordClass::Undecodable(OpRecordError)` (`:118`): the payload is discarded at every production site; only `staging.rs` stringifies it via `encode_op_record`'s `Result`.

### 4. `crates/engine/src/sync/record.rs:22-35` — `RecordSeal.owner_enc_pub` is always derivable from a key the caller already holds

`RecordSeal` pairs a public half with an ephemeral scalar, but the public half is *always* `session.enc_subkey().public()` — the very key `RecordReader::new(session.enc_subkey())` is built from two lines away in `facade.rs`. The engine therefore holds one key and constructs two different wrappers around it, and the type invites a mismatched pair (a record tagged for one key, sealed to another) that has to be prevented by convention.

**Fix:** collapse both into `RecordReader`, which already owns the secret and derives the tag:

```rust
impl RecordReader<'_> {
    pub fn seal(&self, ephemeral: Zeroizing<[u8; 32]>, op: &Op) -> Result<Vec<u8>, OpRecordError>
}
```

`RecordSeal` and free-function `encode_op_record` both disappear; `facade::record_seal()` (`:1651-1670`) shrinks to filling one scalar; `stage_op`'s parameter list loses a type. Tests that seal for a stranger already hold the stranger's `X25519Secret`, so they build a second reader instead — arguably clearer about what they're simulating.

### 5. Comment volume — one invariant restated 9+ times

The "retained record" rule is stated in full at: `CONTEXT.md:57`, `blueprint/engine.md:211-221`, `crates/core/src/seal/op_record.rs:1-20` (module header), `crates/engine/src/sync/record.rs:1-12` (module header, restating core's), `record.rs:113-116` (`RecordClass::Retained`), `record.rs:122-136` (`RetainedReason` + both variants), `rebase.rs:81-83` (`DeadLetterReason::Undecodable`), `rebase.rs` `QueueScan.retained`, `facade.rs:168-173`, `crates/wasm/src/lib.rs:329-331`, `packages/client/src/worker/protocol.ts:60-66`. Eleven statements of one rule. AGENTS.md: *state it once, at its home, and prefer a one-line cross-reference*.

Same pattern for "unmeasurable ≠ full", stated six times: `storage_policy.rs:58-61`, `:66-68`, `:103-104`, `staging.rs` `RejectedStorageUnmeasured` doc, `wasm/src/host.rs:141-146`, `engineWorker.ts:45-53`, plus `blueprint/engine.md:212-214`.

**Fix:** keep the full statement in `CONTEXT.md` / `blueprint/`; everywhere else, one line: `/// See CONTEXT.md "Retained record".` Specific cuts:

- `facade.rs:168-173` → `/// Queue entries held but not readable by this session (CONTEXT.md "Retained record").`
- `record.rs:1-12` → drop paras 2; core's module header already owns that rationale.
- `record.rs:122-136` → one line per variant, or delete with finding 3.
- `wasm/src/host.rs:141-146` and `engineWorker.ts:45-53` → one line each.

### 6. Absence-justifying comments (AGENTS.md explicitly bans these)

- **`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:1018-1022`** — *"Retained records — another account's, or a newer build's format — **are not in this list and never reach removal**"*. Textbook: prose about a path that isn't in the code. The loop iterates `scan.undecodable`; that is already the whole statement. Delete the sentence.
- **`crates/core/src/seal/op_record.rs`, `decode_op_record_header` doc** — *"**Deliberately does not reject** an unrecognised version — that is `open_op_record`'s job."* Explains an absent check. Replace with what it does do: `/// Reads the clear header at any version, without a key.`
- **`crates/core/src/seal/op_record.rs`, `op_record_aad` doc** — *"**Deliberately not an `AadContext`**: that frozen shape binds a node id, scope, and epoch, none of which a local journal entry has."* Defends a type the function doesn't use.
- **`crates/engine/src/storage_policy.rs:88-90`** — *"There is deliberately **no floor-up**…"* Justifies absent code; the test name `a_tiny_headroom_yields_a_tiny_budget_and_never_floors_up` already carries this.
- **`crates/engine/src/sync/record.rs:84-87`** (`classify` doc) — *"version first, tag second, open third, nothing between"* narrates the happy path the next 15 lines plainly show. Keep only the second sentence (why both precede the open).
- **`crates/engine/src/storage_policy.rs:126-128`** — a 2-line comment defending an `#[allow(clippy::assertions_on_constants)]`. Apologia for a lint suppression; drop the comment (the `#[allow]` is self-evident) or drop the test with finding 2.

### 7. Duplicated test fixtures — 6 hand-rolled `StagedContent` builders, 4 copies of one const, 4 copies of a re-framing helper

- `fn staged(...)`: `authored.rs:32`, `record.rs:179`, `op.rs:268`, `tests/sync.rs:70`, `rebase.rs:531` (`staged_k`), `staging.rs:176` (`content_op`). Six variants with three different signatures.
- `const AT: UnixMillis = UnixMillis(0);` **with the identical doc comment** `/// Journal time for ops whose narrative does not turn on it.` at `boot.rs:266`, `overlay.rs:74`, `rebase.rs:528`, `tests/sync.rs:39`.
- "re-frame a record at `OP_RECORD_V + 1`": `record.rs:193` (`at_version`), `staging.rs:412-425` (re-implemented inline, 12 lines), `core/examples/kat_gen.rs:5648` (`reframe_op_record`), `core/src/seal/op_record.rs` tests (inline twice).
- `fn cid(bytes)`/`root_cid(marker)`: `staging.rs:164`, `tests/sync.rs:65`, `op_record.rs:202`.

This repo just did this exact consolidation for head-block fixtures (`7d8c4a3fa test(engine): extract the shared owner-root head-block fixture to testkit`). **Fix:** put `AT`, `staged(marker) -> StagedContent`, `root_cid(marker)`, and `at_version(record, v)` in `crates/engine/src/testkit` (already `#[cfg(feature = "test-kit")]` and reachable from both unit and integration tests). Core's re-framing helper goes next to the KAT generator's `reframe_op_record` rather than being inlined a third and fourth time.

### 8. Near-identical test bodies

- `staging.rs:384` `a_foreign_records_staged_root_is_never_collected` vs `:412` `a_forward_version_records_staged_root_is_never_collected` — identical bodies except how the record is built; both assert `orphan_staging_keys == vec![b"orphan"]`. With an `at_version` helper these become one table-driven test over `[foreign_record(), forward_version_record()]`.
- `record.rs:281` `a_content_record_exposes_its_root_cid_keylessly` and `record.rs:246` `a_forward_version_record_still_yields_its_staged_root` — the second subsumes the first; and `crates/core/src/seal/op_record.rs` `a_content_record_exposes_its_root_cid_without_a_key` proves the same property one crate down.
